Title: Emission Color
Content: Emission Color - Adjust the Emission Color to express retro-reflection and luminous materials which emit light by itself. - Select the fabric item in the Object Browser to apply the Emission Color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and select the color chip next to Material Emission Color. - The Color window will appear allowing you to select the Emission Color. - Click or type in desired values to RGB to apply the desired Emission Color to the fabric.

Title: Refresh Textures
Content: Refresh Texture - After editing and saving the texture image in any image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, and more, click the Refresh button in CLO to apply the changes instantly. - Right-click on the 3D window and select Refresh Textures. - Edit and save the texture image as its original file name in any image editing software. - Navigate back to CLO and right click to select Refresh Textures from the pop-up menu. - The textures applied to Patterns will be updated.

Title: Express Glitter (ver5.0.0)
Content: Objective Express various glitter with different color. Location Object Browser Property Editor (Select Fabric) Material Type Glitter (Render Only) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Property Editor (Select Fabric) Material Type Glitter (Render Only) Note: To preview the glitter, please navigate to the Main Menu Render Render Interactive Render. Refer to the below table and express the desired glitter by modifying the properties. Option Description Glitter Parameters Color Set glitter color. Number Set the number of the glitter particles. Higher the value is, more the glitter particles are, and vice-versa. Saturation Variation Randomize each glitter particle's color. When the value is 0, there's no variation to the color, showing the color set by the user. On the other hand, more color appear when the value is 1. Note: When one of the R, G, B values of the color is dominant, saturation variation occurs within the corresponding color value. In the above case, you may not see various color. To express various color, please set R, G, B values similarly.

Title: [Style Property] Apply Topstitch Texture
Content: Objective Change texture type for Topstitch(es). Note : Texture can only be applied when the type is selected for Texture in the Property Editor. Location Property Editor Texture Search Operation Object Browser Select a Topstitch to add texture image. The selected Topstitch is now being highlighted. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Texture Search The Open File window appears. Select and open desired texture image file. The selected image is now being applied to the selected Topstitch. Note : Not like fabrics, texture image file cannot be applied by Drag &amp Drop for Topstitch.

Title: Elastic
Content: List of Contents Pattern Pattern Outline or Internal Line Objective Apply elastic to the patterns or lines to express details such as E-bands or shirring. Operation Pattern (ver 7.2) In the Library window, click Fabric Elastic folder. In the fabric tab of the Object Browser, select the fabric of the pattern to represent E-band. Property Editor appears. Click the Elastic option on the right side of the Physical Property. Elastic properties appear. Adjust the Elastic properties. Preset Set the default elastic presets. Strength and Stiffness Adjust the strength and stiffness of the elastic. Thickness Set the thickness of the elastic. Pattern Outline or Internal Line Select a outer or internal line with Edit Pattern tool. Property Editor appears. Click the Elastic option to On. Adjust the Elastic properties. Strength Adjust the strength of the elastic. Ratio Adjust the ratio of the elastic. Segment Length Adjusts the elastic ratio when the length value is entered. Total Length If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.

Title: Opacity
Content: Opacity - Adjust the Opacity to express see-through materials. - Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. - Navigate to the Property Editor and adjust Material Opacity. - Adjust the scrollbar or type in desired values to edit the Opacity values. - The materials Opacity will change according to the setting.

Title: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
Content: Objective Use Bending intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately likewise the real fabrics. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Bending-Weft/Warp Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity Note: Adjust Bending for bias by using Bending - Bias (ver.5.1.0).

Title: Open Textures in AI / PS (ver 6.1)
Content: Objective Open the texture image applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop. Location Fabric Property button right to each map. Operation Click the tool/menu indicated. The pop-up menu appears. Click Add Another App menu. Select Application window appears. Select the executable file (EXE) of the application to be added. Click Open button. The texture will then open in that application and the application will be added to the list of the pop-up menu as well. Save the edited texture in the application, return to CLO, then right-click on the background in the 3D window. Click Refresh Textures (F5). The edited texture image appears. Note: Once you click Open with Another App menu, you can only execute the selected application without adding it to the pop-up menu. User Settings Other you can register or delete the application that is opening textures.

Title: AI Texture Generator (ver 7.3)
Content: List of Contents Open Generate Apply Objective Easily type in keywords to generate different texture images to choose from to create new textures. Location Object Browser Fabric Tap Operation Open Click the tool/menu in Location. Fabric Property Materials Click AI Texture Generator button on the right side of the Basic Parameters. AI Texture Generator window appears. Generate Set options, enter prompts, and click the Generate button. Fabric Type Select the fabric type. The pattern is generated on the texture of the selected fabric. Content Type Select contents type. Style Select the style of the texture image. Pattern Select the repeated-pattern type. Pattern Size Only adjusts the size of the pattern while maintaining the size of the texture. Text Prompt Enter the prompts. Currently, prompts can only be entered in English. Writing Tips: List the words. Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. Emphasize certain words. If parentheses are used in the word you want to emphasize, it takes up more weight. Parentheses on certain words take more weight. Weight increase rate:(word) 1.1times, ((word)) 1.21times. Maintain Prompt Even if the same prompts are used, the AI texture image is generated newly each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Result button may update the prompts while maintaining the characteristics of the previously generated result as much as possible. Note: It may differ from the existing result depending on the addition or change of the prompts. Random The sample prompt is randomly applied. History Previously generated images with prompts are recorded as histories. The histories are remained until CLO Software is closed. Note : It may take a while to create when there are many users at the same time. Apply Click the Apply button below when the AI Texture is completely generated. The result is applied to the 3D garment, and can be checked in advance. BUT, the fabric must be applied to it.

Title: Adjust Rendering Thickness
Content: List of Contents Fabric Unit Pattern Unit Objective Set Fabric thickness for a Garment in the 3D Garment window. Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as default vale, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. Note: To see the rendering thickness, 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on Thick Textured Surface . Location Fabric Unit Object Browser Fabric Fabric Item Property Editor Thickness Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Rendering Operation Fabric Unit Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Fabric Item Property Editor Thickness Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Rendering Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

Title: Graphic Properties
Content: List of Contents Properties Options Objective Set the graphic properties. Location 2D Toolbar Transform Graphic Operation Properties Graphic Style Object Browser Click a graphic style in the Graphic Tab The selected graphic's properties appear in the Property Editor. Set the properties of the graphic style. Properties Description Information Name/Item No. Enter a name or an item number of the graphic. Classification Assign the graphic type among Embroidery, Logo, Print, Wash (Jeanologia). Teckpack (CLO-SET) Check whether to include the graphic in the tech pack. Assign the classification of the graphic as per its purpose. Material Print Type (ver 2024.1) Set the print type of the graphic (Crack, Vintage Distress, Golden Foil). When you select the Blend with Base Fabric type, all PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness maps) of the fabric applied to the pattern are automatically applied and blended with the fabric. Otherwise, you can selectively apply only specific maps by checking the 'Use the same map as the fabric' option for each map. Set the graphic's material, texture, color, and transparency. Graphic Transformation Adjust the width and height of the graphic to transform its size. Individual Graphic Click the tool/menu in Location. Select a graphic to set properties. The properties of the graphic will appear in the Property Editor. Set individual properties of the graphic as needed. Properties Description Graphic Configuration Face Place the graphic on the front, back, or both sides. Tile Repeat the graphic in its original size along the X-axis, Y-axis, or across the entire pattern. Over Seamline Place the graphic on the seam of patterns. Note: - Graphic does not appear when the difference of the seam is over the allowable extent. - Graphic may not be matching when it is placed over the curves. It this case, deactivate this option and adjust the graphic manually. - Graphics are also created for patterns sewn in two layers, such as pockets. (ver 7.2 ) Graphic Transformation Adjust the rotation angle and Z-offset of graphic. 2D Measurements Click the desired measurement option to check the position within the 2D pattern in dimensions. Options Click the tool/menu in Location. Right click on the 2D graphic. A right-click popup menu appears. Apply options as needed. Options Descriptions Delete Delete the selected graphic. Copy/ Paste Copy, Paste, and Mirror Paste the selected graphic. Order (2D) Set the placement order of the graphic. Rotate Set the rotation angle of the graphic. Tile Repeat the graphic in its original size along the X-axis, Y-axis, or across the entire pattern. Revert to Original Size Restore the transformed graphic to its original size. Filip Flip the graphic horizontally or vertically. Trace as Internal Shape (ver 2024.0) Trace the graphic as an internal shape according to its outline. Note: The clearer the image, the more accurately it is recognized. For complex and colored images, tracing is based on the outermost outline. Custom Measurements (ver 2024.0) Measure the distance from a specific point of the graphic to its outline and create a measurement. The created measurement is displayed in the Property Editor, and you can rename or delete it as needed.

Title: Adjust Buckling Ratio
Content: Objective Use this function to reflect the tendency of Fabric trying to preserve its shape then being bent when applying certain amount of force. The closer the Buckling Ratio gets to 100 percent (%), the more it becomes easily bendable fabric such as silk and jersey. On the other hand, the closer the ration gets to 0 percent (%), the more it becomes less bendable fabric such as denim and wool. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Buckling Ratio Note: Adjust Buckling Ratio for bias by using Buckling Ratio - Bias (ver.5.1.0).

Title: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
Content: Objective Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Buckling Stiffness-Weft/Warp Note: Adjust Buckling Stiffness for bias by using Buckling Stiffness - Bias (ver.5.1.0).

Title: Piping Property Setting
Content: Objective Modify the physical Piping properties at Property Editor. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move tool or Edit Piping tool. Operation Click the tool / Menu in the Location. Select a piping. Piping properties appear in the Property Editor. Set properties as needed. Property Discription Information Enter the name and Item.No of the selected piping, and check the length. Dimension Adjust the Width and Particle Distance of the selected piping. Displays the line length of selected Piping. Finishing (ver 7.3) Set wheter the ends of pining are closed. Hide Shows/hides selected Piping. Fabric Apply fabric to the selected Piping Piping's fabric texture can be edited using the Edit Texture tool.

Title: [Mode] Emulator
Content: Objective Digitize new fabric and save as a file in Emulator Mode. Location Main Menu Change the mode at the top-right corner EMULATOR Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Change the mode at the top-right corner EMULATOR Emulator window appears. Input the property value of the fabric measured step by step according to the description on the left screen. Note: Select Enter All Values to skip to the last page where users may manually enter all values without going through previous steps. (ver 5.1.0) Press Compute once finish putting the value and wait until automatic calculation for the fabric property is completed. Save the calculated fabric as .zfab file.

Title: Select Binding
Content: Objective Edit Binding Properties. Location Main Menu Materials Binding Select Binding 3D Toolbar Select Binding Note: 3D toolbar Select bindings with the Select/Move tool. Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. The line segment for which the binding was created is displayed. Select the Binding to be edited. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Configure each property as needed referring to below table. Option Description Name Rename Binding's name. Line Length Check Binding's length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. Type Under Bindings are placed under the Patterns to express Inside Bindings. Over Bindings are placed over the Patterns. Both (ver 7.0) Bindings are placed both direction of the Patterns. Dimension Width Adjust selected Binding's width. (1~50mm) Length Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50% ~ 200%) or a specific value. Particle Distance Edit selected Binding's Particle Distance (4~20mm) Add'l Thickness - Collision Adjust Binding's Add'l Thickness - Collision. Fabric Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. Grain Direction Bias/ Warp/ Custom Choose among Bias, Warp, or Custom for the Binding's grain direction. Angle Manually insert Angle value to set the Binding's grain direction. Topstitch Add Topstitch to the Binding. The Topstitch option shows the styles which are added in the Topstitch tab of Object Browser. Sewing Line Type Edit Binding's Sewing Line Type. Extend Set whether to extend the binding after creating it on a part of the line segment. Note: Binding Extension is not possible in the following cases. When the angle of both segments are more than 180 degrees based on the binding start/end point. Right-click on the Binding to be edited. Option Description Delete Delete selected Binding. Reset Arrangement Reset Binding's position. Use this option to fix unstable simulations. Deactivate / Activate Deactivate or activate selected Binding. Freeze / Unfreeze Freeze or unfreeze selected Binding. Flip Normal The selected Binding's face flips to the other side.

Title: Palette
Content: List of Contents Color Palette Color Swatch Color Palette Palette Library Color Palette - Import Color Palettes from Adobe Illustrator or Adobe Photoshop or create a custom Color Palette to utilize during the design process. Color Swatch Add Color Swatch - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the desired color from the Color Browser window or the Color Swatch Library. - Click the Add Button. - The selected color will be added as a swatch. Rename Color Swatch - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the Display button on the furthest right top of the Color Palette. - The Color Palette display will change and each color swatchs name will appear. - Double click the color name to edit. - Type in the desired color name and select OK. Re-order Color Swatch - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material &gt Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click and drag the color swatch to be reordered. - Release the mouse to complete the modification. Color Palette Reset Color Palette - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material &gt Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the Reset Custom Palette button on the right top of the Color Palette. - The dialogue informing that all color swatches will be removed will pop-up. Select Reset. - All color swatches will be deleted from the Color Palette. Save Color Palette - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material &gt Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the Save as Palette button on the right top of the Color Palette. - Designate the saving path and file name, and then select Save. - The custom Color Palette will be saved as .aco files. Open Color Palette - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the Open Palette button on the right top of the color palette. The Open Palette window will pop-up allowing you to choose an option for importing a Color Palette: to delete and create a new Color Palette, click the New button. On the other hand, to add a new Color Palette, select the Add Button. - Locate the Color Palette file and click Open. - The desired Color Palette will be loaded. Change color Palette Display - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - There are total of three display styles and each change with the click of the Display button on the right top of the Color Palette. Palette Library Create Palette Library - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the + button on the right top of the Palette Library. - The Open File window will pop-up. - The Open File window will pop-up. - The selected Palette file will be added to the library as a new tab. Copy to Color Palette - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - Click the Copy to Custom Palette button on the right bottom of the Palette Library. - The Copy to Custom Palette window will pop-up allowing you to choose an option for importing a Color Palette: to delete and create a new Color Palette, click the New button. On the other hand, to add a new Color Palette, select the Add Button. - The color swatches in the selected Color Palette will be copied to the Custom Palette. Change Color Palette Display - Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material Color. - The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. - There are total of three display styles and each change with the click of the Display button on the right top of the Color Palette.

Title: Refresh Texture
Content: Objective Edit texture images with an image editing tool (Photoshop, Illustrator) and save over the original image with the same name and file location, press Refresh button to instantly apply the changes of the Fabric's texture images. Location Main Menu 3D/2D Window Background Right-click Pop-up Menu Refresh Textures

Title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)
Content: Objective Use the Property Editor to resize the texture applied to the Patterns. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric (Select the Desired One) Property Editor Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric (Select the Desired One) Property Editor The selected Fabric's properties appear in the Property Editor. Find the Transformation option which only appears when a texture is applied to a Pattern. Option Description Angle Type in the rotating angle. Width Set the texture width. % (ver5.0.0) Configure the texture width with percentage. Height Set the texture height. % (ver5.0.0) Configure the texture height with percentage. Lock Aspect Ratio Lock the width and height ratio.

Title: Unified Map 6.1
Content: Objective When a pattern construction constrains a print layout, apply the texture using Unified Map. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab On the right button of Fabric Item Texture Repeat / Unified Map. Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Mapping Operation Click the tool/ menu indicated. Use Unified Map to apply the texture differently. Set the specific options of the Unified Map. Repeat U Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the U direction. Repeat V Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the V direction. Note: Once you have applied the Unified Fabric Map, the Edit Texture Tool will only rotate the Grain-line, NOT the Texture.

Title: Import AxF file
Content: Objective Express textures by using the AxF file of X-Rite that express realistic fabric materials with various maps extracted by three-dimensional scanning of fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric Operation Click the tool/ menu indicated in Location. Right click the fabric item and Import/ Import (Add). Open File window appears. Select the AxF file and click Open. Fabric property is converted into the property of AxF file. When using Import (Add), the properties that have already set are retained, only the properties that are not present are changed to the corresponding Axf file. (Ex: When having texture only, the other maps are applied such as Normal, Alpha, or etc) Note: You can drag and drop the AxF file to Fabric in Object Browser, 2D Pattern, and 3D Garment.

Title: Adjust Density
Content: Objective Use this function to express the weight ratio per unit (m²). The higher the value, the heavier the fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Density

Title: Complete Nonlinear Simulation
Content: Objective This function allows more accurate Simulation on fabric stretch (ver3.0.0). It is especially effective for longer Garments. Note: This is available from ver3.0.0 onward. Location 3D Garment Window Right-click Pop-up Menu Simulation Properties Property Editor Nonlinear Simulation Operation Follow the indicated guideline below and check the Nonlinear Simulation On: 3D Garment Window Simulation Property Editor Preset Complete (Nonlinear) Fabric strength and elongation are now being simulated more accurately.

Title: Apply Texture
Content: List of Contents Apply Texture Add Texture Apply with Desired Map Type Apply Texture - Apply an image file to the Fabric style to express fabrics texture. - Select a Fabric style from the Fabric tab under the Object Browser. Then, navigate to the Property Editor Material Texture. Add Texture Via Property Editor - Select a Fabric style from the Fabric tab under the Object Browser. - Click the Browser button next to the Texture option. - The chosen image is applied as texture. Via Drag&ampDrop - From the PCs Browser window, click, drag and drop the image file to the Browse button next to the Texture option. The image file is applied as texture. Apply with Desired Map Type - From the PCs Browser window, drag and drop an image file to an object where the image should be applied to. - The Texture Map Type window appears. Choose the desired Map type and select OK. Note: Normal and Roughness map are retained even if the texture is deleted.

Title: Specular Color
Content: List of Contents Specular Color Apply Specular Color Adjust Shininess Specular Color - The Specular Color is the color of the light directly reflected from the fabric used to express glossy materials such as enamel. Apply Specular Color - Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. - Navigate to the Property Editor and select the color chip next to the Material Specular Color. - When the color window appears, select the desired Specular Color. - Brighter the Specular Color is, glossier the fabric will become. Adjust Shininess - Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. - Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material Specular Color to see its child menus. Locate the Shininess option. - Move the scroll bar to adjust the gloss of the fabric. Higher the Shininess value is, glossier the fabric will become, like enamel. However, on the contrast, lower the Shininess value is, more regularly the gloss will spread on the surface of the fabric, like lame.

Title: Vizoo File Compatibility
Content: Objective CLO is compatible with Vizoo 3D which scans actual material information (Color/Specular/Normal Map). Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Right-click on a Fabric style. Select Import xTex File from the menu and load the relevant xTex file.

Title: Adjust Internal Damping
Content: Objective Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. Note: Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Internal Damping

Title: Print on Fabric (ver 6.0)
Content: List of Contents Add Print Set Print Properties Copy Print Save Print (PRT) Objective Print various patterns on Fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric tab Operation Add Print Click Add Print to the right of the Fabric item. Open file window appears. Select the desired image. A print item is added under the fabric item. Set Print Property Click the Print Item under the Fabric item. Print Properties appear in the Property Editor. Edit the Print Properties as needed. Properties Description Information Name the print by clicking the name of the fabric item or right-clicking on it and select Rename. You can also change the name in the Property Editor. Configuration Face Set the orientation(Front, Back, and Both) of the fabric to be printed. Repeat Type Set the Repeat Type (Block, Half Drop, Brick, Diamond, Stripe)of the pattern to be printed Space Set the space between the images of the X / Y-axis. Shift Shift the images along the X / Y-axis. Type Set the Type of Print Image. If you set the option to use the same normal map as the fabric, the normal map of the fabric is also applied to the print. (ver 7.3) Transformation Set the width, height and angle of the Print Image. Note: Edit Texture tool edits the texture of the fabric and the print image together and if the fabric to which the print image was added has no texture, the Texture Editor tool cannot be used Open/Save Print Properties can be saved or opened as a PRT file. When saving as a fabric file(ZFAB), the print properties are also saved. Copy Print Click the fabric item to copy. Click the Copy Print to the right of the Print item to be copied. The print item is copied to the fabric.

Title: Object Browser
Content: View and edit items used in both 3D and 2D Windows such as Scene, Fabric, Button, Buttonhole, Topstitch, and Puckering. Scene Scene tab is the primary, fastest, and most streamlined tool for finding or selecting object. It lets you quickly review a list of all objects and its structure in the 3D and 2D Windows. The list is in the order of object created, but when you click on Name, the object list is sorted A to Z (1 to 10). Once you click again, the list is reordered and sorted Z to A (10 to 1). Fabric Fabric Tab represents the menu for Fabric. Users can select, add, copy and reset Fabric. Click and drag to reorder Fabric styles as desired (ver4.1.0). Button Button Tab displays a list of button items. User can select, add, and copy Button. Buttonhole Buttonhole Tab displays a list of Buttonhole items. Users can select, add, and copy Buttonholes Topstitch Topstitch Tab displays a list of Topstitch items. Users can select, add, and copy Topstitch. Puckering Puckering Tab displays a list of Puckering items. Users can select, add, and copy Puckerings.

Title: Topstitch Face Setting
Content: Objective Select the face of Topstitch. Location Object Browser Topstitch Topstitch Property Editor Face Explanation Topstitch is only set for the front of the Fabric. Topstitch is only set for the back of the Fabric. Topstitch is set for the both sides of the Fabric. Note: Topstitch placed on the back of the Fabric do not appear in the 2D window (ver4.2.0).
